mechanism_narrative: A continued recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT over the next month will raise weekday foot traffic and spill over into RETAIL_REC, because more commuting increases stop-by shopping and meal trips.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -9.3 to -3.7 and TRANSIT from -9.4 to -5.3 across the snapshot
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise over the next four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior four-week mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A further rise in RESIDENTIAL time above 6% signals more time spent near home, which will reduce discretionary retail visits within the next week and push RETAIL_REC lower relative to the prior four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed elevated at 6.0-7.3 in all four weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above 6% but RETAIL_REC rises over the next week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility drops below -15% after being less negative the prior week, outdoor leisure demand is shifting away from shared venues and toward home-based activity, which will pull RETAIL_REC down over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -15% week-on-week or remains below -15% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -12.0 to -17.0 and then to -14.6 in the snapshot
failure_condition: If PARKS stays below -15% but RETAIL_REC does not decline versus the last two-week average, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT recovers faster than WORKPLACES, more non-work trips are being enabled without an equivalent office rebound, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks through shopping and dining access.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by at least 2 points while WORKPLACES improves by less than 1 point in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -9.4 to -5.3 while WORKPLACES improved from -9.3 to -3.7 in the latest two weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT keeps improving faster than WORKPLACES but RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines over the next month, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GROCERY_PHARM alongside a rebound in WORKPLACES indicates broader trip generation and errand chaining, which will translate into higher RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 31.6 to 37.6 while WORKPLACES rose from -4.6 to -3.7 by t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES both rise but RETAIL_REC does not improve within two weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Once RETAIL_REC has already been depressed for four weeks while RESIDENTIAL stays above 6%, pent-up shopping demand is exhausted and retail mobility will remain below its recent average over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC remains below -10% for four consecutive weeks while RESIDENTIAL stays above 6%
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC stayed between -13.7 and -10.9 while RESIDENTIAL stayed between 6.0 and 7.3
failure_condition: If prolonged low RETAIL_REC and elevated RESIDENTIAL are followed by a four-week retail rebound, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES will first lift weekday access and then retail visits, producing higher RETAIL_REC after one month; the effect weakens if either series reverses.
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved at t-0w relative to t-2w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue recovering but RETAIL_REC is not higher than the last four-week mean after four weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS rebounds while GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated, weekend outdoor substitution and errand clustering will reduce incremental retail visits, causing RETAIL_REC to soften within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 2 points from the prior week while GROCERY_PHARM stays above 35%
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -17.0 to -14.6 while GROCERY_PHARM stayed elevated near 35-38
failure_condition: If PARKS rebounds and GROCERY_PHARM remains high but RETAIL_REC increases over the next week, the hypothesis is false.
